Each row in a dataset is a sample. A feature is information available at prediction time, and a label is the desired answer. To predict duration when a Task is created, task type and description length can be features; actual_minutes is the answer you want to predict.

Data leakage occurs when the answer or future information enters the features. finished_at and final duration are unknown when a Task is created; using them can make evaluation look excellent while making real-world use ineffective.

In supervised learning, samples have training answers: regression produces numeric answers such as minutes, and classification produces categories such as spam. Unsupervised learning examines data structure without that target label, for example by grouping Task descriptions.

A baseline is a simple reference for comparison. A constant mean model predicts the training set's mean duration for every task; it does not inspect features. Its parameter is mean_train, and MAE is the mean absolute difference between predictions and actual answers, measured in minutes.

A Tensor is a multidimensional array with a shape, dtype, and device. A gradient is the derivative of loss with respect to a parameter. backward computes gradients from the computation graph, and optimizer.step changes parameters according to the chosen rule; backward alone does not update weights. This distinction is essential for debugging the loop.

PyTorch accumulates gradients in grad; in ordinary per-batch training, zero_grad should run before backward. Validation has no step and should run with eval and no_grad. Decreasing training loss does not guarantee improved validation at every epoch.

A tokenizer converts text into vocabulary-unit IDs; a token is not necessarily a word or character. An embedding is a learned vector table for these IDs, and positional information is supplied according to the architecture. Token count affects sequence length and memory use.

Self-attention combines information from visible positions with input-dependent weights; multi-head attention uses multiple computation spaces. A generative decoder-only model usually uses a causal mask to avoid seeing future tokens, while an encoder such as BERT has a different visibility contract and training objective.

Fine-tuning changes weights for a new task. LoRA often freezes base weights and trains low-rank parameters; QLoRA uses a low-precision base with adapters. Quantization reduces numeric representation precision and is not by itself equivalent to training or new learning.

Memory use is more than the weights file size; activations, gradients, optimizer, batch size, and sequence length also matter. You can practice the method with a CPU and small model. Choosing a model with billions of parameters merely because it is 4-bit does not guarantee that it fits in VRAM.
